description:
As the US-Israeli war with Iran enters its third week, President Donald Trump renewed calls this weekend for countries to work with the US to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Iran's military has vowed to strike US-linked oil and gas infrastructure in the Middle East if more of its own energy sites are attacked. This follows a US operation targeting Kharg Island, a key Iranian export hub.

Here's a roundup of retired US generals analyzing the second week of the Iran war.

15:54 Gen. David Petraeus on Marine unit deployment, Trump admin war planning & achieving objectives
24:42 Brig. Gen. Mark Kimmitt on where the war stands

author: CNN
description:
Ever since the US and Israel struck Iran, the jump in oil and gas prices has become a major focus for markets and consumers alike. But that’s only the top of a long list of goods that stand to get more expensive.

US mortgage rates climbed this week, undoing some of the welcomed progress in housing affordability. Prices for perishables – dairy, fruits, vegetables, fish – will rise first. Airfares could come next. But, eventually, if fuel prices remain high, many goods that are transported on a truck, plane or ship will go up in cost.

7:44 If you're booked on a Gulf airline, should you reconsider?
10:16 Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA) on war's effect on grocery prices

Watch more CNN here: https://cnn.it/4kh5RPe

#IranWar #Prices #News
title: Iran war hikes US costs of mortgages, flights, groceries & more

author: CNN
description:
The Pentagon is deploying a Marine Expeditionary Unit to the Middle East, a rapid response unit typically comprised of around 2,500 Marines and sailors, three officials familiar with the matter told CNN.

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump said tonight the United States bombed “every military target” on Iran’s Kharg Island and threatened to attack the island’s oil infrastructure if Iran continues blocking ships from traversing the Strait of Hormuz.

Kharg Island is a five-mile-stretch of land off the Iranian coast that had seemingly been left untouched during the first two weeks of the war with Iran. The critical island handles roughly 90% of the country’s crude exports.
